findings.text: follow-on: the migration's composition and destination-resolution scripts (scan_dispositions.py, assemble_rows.py, build_fragment.py, emit_fragment.py, check_destinations.py) live only in the run directory and were not committed, so the 85-row table's exact assembly is not reproducible from the repository; only the zero-hiding predicate result is. A later backfill or re-review would have to rebuild the instruments. Consider committing the checker under tests/ or a tool path if the migration is ever re-run.

follow-on: s4's done-when asks for the disposition table in this plan's landed record; the node correctly delivered an evidence fragment and left closure to the coordinator, so the coordinator still owes the landing (record the table into the plan's landed record, resolve the driving followup, advance the plan status) before s4 can be called done.

justifications.durability: the deliverable is a committed artifact whose headline claims are reproducible from the repository: the predicate and the positive-control test travel with the code, and the fragment is self-describing (base sha, command, logs named). Docked because the composition and destination-resolution instruments - scan_dispositions.py, assemble_rows.py, build_fragment.py, emit_fragment.py, check_destinations.py - live only in the run directory and are uncommitted, so a later reader can re-derive the predicate result but cannot re-run the exact 85-row assembly or its destination check; the 85-row set is therefore not independently reproducible from the repo even though the zero-hiding measure is.
justifications.evidence: the core claim is independently reproduced: at e85fb9cd8 the predicate classifies all 41 open followups as pointers and none as hiding, and the committed positive-control suite (tests/test_a_followup_that_hides_work_is_found.py) passes 11/11 on re-run; the synthetic own-plan no-section control returns hides-work (no-section), so the zero is not a blind instrument. The negative control holds: the destination checker catches 3 of 3 synthetic bad rows (§99, a missing plan, a missing decision) while all 85 real rows resolve. I spot-checked independently: all 15 cited commit shas resolve to commits (4d2780ee7, 8512e8982, d711aee1e, d4eee48b, abb4f98bf, 469720867, c165a45ac, b5012383a, e35585e5a, b4739ec79, e7ae7304f, 034172a37, d3245613e, f65cc8edf, 0bdd53a17), the sampled section anchors exist (a-brief-should-not-cost-what-it-names s8; crew-observability-truth s24,s28,s29,s36,s37,s39; work-is-a-section-not-a-followup s4), the three held-row destinations match their outcomes verbatim (f-ifv-002 -> the-restarted-server-meets-its-shipped-measures s1; f-nso-002 -> s2; f-pcg-002 -> scoring-should-stop-a-promotion s12), and audit-doc returns OK on the fragment. Docked because the roadmap-level evidence is the node's own log alone (a full `reckon roadmap` re-run was not possible under this node's fence) and the fragment does not spell out how the 5 met rows that neither cite the migration in their outcome nor are the three held rows were selected.
justifications.fit: the change follows s4 exactly: the four dispositions are s4's four (section, move, decision, met), the rows name where the work went (section anchor, plan, decision key or commit), and the fragment declares the measure s4's done-when asks for (zero followups that hide work). It writes no plan state and correctly leaves the plan's status and driving followup to the coordinator, matching its scope grant (a fragment plus a figures directory, no figure needed for a table node).
justifications.goal_fidelity: the node's deliverable - a table disposing every followup that hid work - is met and independently reproduced: the fragment carries 85 rows over the four dispositions s4 names (51 section, 13 move, 6 decision, 15 met; sum 85, no duplicate plan+id), and the core measure reproduces off-tree (classify_followup over docs/plans at e85fb9cd8 yields 41 open followups, 0 hiding, 41 pointers, reasons implementable-section 21 / other-plan 20). Docked because the disposition table currently lives in an evidence fragment rather than in the plan's landed record, which s4's done-when names, so the coordinator still owes the landing; and the fragment lead's phrasing '85 open followups that the roadmap's predicate called hiding work' overstates the row set - the rows are citation-derived resolved followups (77 cite the migration in their outcome; 8 more exist without citing it), while the predicate at the revision read reports zero hiding. Both are coordinator-owned next steps, not node defects.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff writes exactly one path within the node's grant (docs/evidence/fragments/work-is-a-section-not-a-followup/the-hidden-work-dispositions-are-tabled.html, 129 insertions, one file), writes no figure and edits no other plan, leaves the worktree clean at the head commit, commits with a conventional subject and a body stating what changed and why, carries no AI trailer, and uses no plan or stage labels in names or comments.
